lines.text: Golden kingdoms, slave forts on the shore, and the first colony south of the Sahara to win its freedom. This is the story of Ghana.
The name comes from an old empire further north, rich from the trade in gold and salt. Modern Ghana borrowed it in 1957.
In 1482 the Portuguese built Elmina Castle on the coast. It would become a hub of the Atlantic slave trade.
Inland, Asante and Ewe weavers made kente, bright cloth of narrow strips whose patterns each carry a meaning.
Along the shore more forts went up. At Cape Coast Castle, captives were held before being shipped across the ocean.
In the forests, Osei Tutu was born, who would found the Ashanti Empire.
Kumasi grew as the Ashanti capital, home of the king, the Asantehene.
United under Osei Tutu and the sacred Golden Stool, the Ashanti grew wealthy on gold and captives, and fought the British for decades.
The British claimed the coast as the Gold Coast colony, and pushed slowly inland.
Yaa Asantewaa, queen mother of Ejisu, would become the face of Ashanti resistance.
In 1900, when the British demanded the Golden Stool, she led the Ashanti into war. They lost, and she was exiled.
Kwame Nkrumah, born in 1909, would lead the movement to end British rule.
Kofi Annan was born in Kumasi in 1938. He would lead the United Nations and win the Nobel Peace Prize.
That same year John Kufuor was born, a future president whose election marked a peaceful handover of power.
Nana Akufo-Addo, born in 1944, would serve as president for eight years.
Jerry Rawlings, an air force officer, would twice seize power, and then lead Ghana back to democracy.
In 1949 Nkrumah founded the Convention People's Party, and pressed hard for self-rule.
On the sixth of March 1957, the Gold Coast became Ghana, the first country south of the Sahara to win its independence.
John Mahama, born in 1958, returned to the presidency in 2025.
Abedi Pele, born in 1964, was crowned African footballer of the year three times.
In 1965 the Akosombo Dam closed on the Volta, creating the largest man-made lake in the world.
From gold and forts to freedom, Ghana showed a continent its way to independence.
